subject: Advisory: Intermittent partial responses (streaming truncation) observed in US-West
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@novaplace.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 17, 2027 at 09:02 AM -0700
Subject: Advisory: Intermittent partial responses (streaming truncation) observed in US-West

Hi Jane —

Heads up: between ~08:30–09:00 PT this morning we saw a spike of requests in the US-West region where streaming generation responses ended prematurely (the model stopped producing output mid-response). We estimate the incident window at 08:28–09:03 PT.

Impact summary:~
- A subset of streaming and long-form generation requests (~5–7% of traffic for affected model variants) returned truncated outputs (partial payloads) rather than full generations.
- Non-streaming and short-turn chat traffic were largely unaffected.
- Requests routed to fallback variants after 08:45 PT saw restored behavior.

What we did immediately:~
- Automatically activated fallback routing for streaming endpoints in US-West to a compatible model variant at 08:45 PT.
- Throttled a small subset of aggressive prefetch/prefill work queues to reduce KV cache churn.
- Opened a high-priority triage and are collecting request traces and logs (attached: incident-logs-0817.csv).

Action for you: no action required from NovaPlace at the moment. If you observed any customer-facing failures or have example request IDs, please reply with them and we’ll prioritize.

We’ll follow up with a technical summary and a postmortem draft tomorrow. Apologies for the disruption — we know partial outputs can be disruptive to user flows and we’re treating this as a high priority.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-logs-0817.csv (log stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 17, 2027 at 09:15 AM -0700
Subject: RE: Advisory: Intermittent partial responses (streaming truncation) observed in US-West

Soojin — quick technical notes from triage: we reproduced the symptom locally and correlated it with a KV-cache flush path that can trigger when a prefix cache eviction occurs mid-stream. In a specific timing window, the runtime would issue an early buffer flush which the streaming layer treated as an end-of-sequence event, causing truncated frames to be sent to clients.

Root cause hypothesis: a recently deployed prefetch optimization (deployed 2027-08-10) increases aggressive prefix caching for high-concurrency customers. Under a short burst pattern the eviction policy combined with an asynchronous flush race caused the streaming sink to signal completion prematurely.

Immediate mitigations applied (~08:40–08:50 PT):
- Disabled the aggressive prefetch config for US-West pools.
- Rolled a small patch to make the streaming sink resilient to mid-stream cache flushes (mitigation flagged as hotfix; refs in mitigation-patch-refs.txt).
- Increased observability on streaming frame completion events and added counters for early-termination.

Status: patch deployed 09:00 PT; observed truncated rate dropped to baseline (<0.1%) by 09:10 PT. Collecting full traces for the postmortem.

Next: finalize rollback/forward plan for the prefetch optimization (likely a controlled rollout with a backpressure safety limit) and publish a short postmortem tomorrow.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-patch-refs.txt (patch references and commit ids)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 17, 2027 at 10:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Advisory: Intermittent partial responses (streaming truncation) observed in US-West

Jane — thanks for the prompt note. Quick numbers from our trace set:~
- Window: 08:28–09:03 PT.
- Estimated fraction of NovaPlace requests impacted (based on routing and customer tags): ~6% of streaming-generation calls in the window.
- Affected model variants: redwood/gpt-medium-epoch2 (streaming-enabled routes); non-streaming endpoints unaffected.

I’ve attached a CSV with a sampled set of request IDs and timestamps (incident-logs-0817.csv). If you can confirm a few IDs from your support queue we’ll correlate server-side logs and confirm there was no input or output corruption beyond truncation.

We’ll follow up with a fuller postmortem with timeline and long-term mitigations by tomorrow afternoon.

— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@novaplace.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Aug 18, 2027 at 02:30 PM -0700
Subject: Postmortem: US-West partial streaming response gap (2027-08-17)

TL;DR: A race between aggressive prefix prefetch eviction and the streaming sink caused early termination of streaming frames for a subset of requests in US-West. Impacted customers saw truncated outputs (no data leakage). Truncation rate peaked at ~6% for affected streaming calls during 08:28–09:03 PT.

Timeline (abridged):
- 08:28 PT: first anomalous early-termination metric alert from streaming counters.
- 08:33 PT: customers report truncated outputs.
- 08:40 PT: triage, fallback routing enabled.
- 08:45 PT: aggressive prefetch feature toggled off for US-West.
- 09:00 PT: hotfix deployed to streaming sink to ignore mid-stream cache flush signals.
- 09:10 PT: truncated rate returned to baseline (<0.1%).

Root cause: interaction between a prefetch optimization (reducing cold-starts) and the existing eviction/flush path. Under short, high-concurrency bursts the eviction path emitted a flush event that was wrongly interpreted by the streaming layer as completion.

Corrective actions (short-term):
- Revert aggressive prefetch rollout for affected pools and deploy the sink fix to all regions (complete).
- Add a safety throttle on prefetch workqueues to limit concurrency bursts.
- Raise sampling of streaming-frame completion traces for 72 hours.

Longer-term actions:
- Refactor streaming sink to separate "cache flush" events from "stream end" signals and add stronger invariants in the runtime.
- Build a canary for prefetch changes with targeted traffic patterns to stress eviction.
- Add customer-level tagging to improve per-customer impact estimates in real time.

If you’d like a scheduled call to walk through the traces or a copy of the longer postmortem draft, I can schedule today. Attached: postmortem-draft-0818.md.

— Ben
